note: 拾词原创的考试题型模拟阅读，非历年考试原文

papers.label: 中考 · 记叙文
papers.title: The Lost Library Card
paras: Last Friday, Leo found a library card on the floor of the school bus.
上周五，利奥在校车的地板上捡到一张图书馆借书卡。
The name on it was Mia Chen, a girl from Class Three.
卡上的名字是米娅·陈，三班的一个女孩。
Leo did not know her, and he was too shy to talk to strangers.
利奥不认识她，而且他太害羞，不敢和陌生人说话。
At first, he wanted to give the card to his teacher.
起初，他想把卡交给老师。
Then he noticed a small note on the back: "Please return. My grandma's book is waiting."
接着他注意到卡背面有一张小纸条：“请归还。我奶奶的书还在等着。”
Leo was curious, so he decided to find Mia himself.
利奥很好奇，于是决定自己去找米娅。
During the lunch break, he walked to Class Three and asked for her.
午休时，他走到三班去找她。
Mia was very happy to see the card.
米娅看到卡非常高兴。
She explained that her grandmother could not see well, so every week Mia borrowed large-print books and read them aloud to her.
她解释说，她奶奶视力不好，所以米娅每周都借大字版的书，读给奶奶听。
Without the card, she could not borrow this week's book.
没有这张卡，她就借不了这周的书。
The next Monday, Mia gave Leo a bookmark she had made.
下个星期一，米娅送给利奥一张她自己做的书签。
On it she wrote, "Thank you for being brave."
上面写着：“谢谢你这么勇敢。”
Leo smiled. He had never thought of himself as brave before.
利奥笑了。他以前从来没觉得自己勇敢。

qs.q: Where did Leo find the library card?
qs.why: 第一句：found a library card on the floor of the school bus。

qs.q: Why did Leo decide to find Mia himself?
o: The note on the card made him curious.
He wanted to make new friends.
qs.why: 看到卡背面的纸条后，Leo was curious, so he decided to find Mia himself。

qs.q: Why did Mia borrow large-print books every week?
o: To read them to her grandmother.
Because she could not see well.
qs.why: 她奶奶视力不好，米娅借大字版书 read them aloud to her。看不清的是奶奶，不是米娅。

qs.q: What can we learn about Leo from the last paragraph?
o: He was still afraid of strangers.
He wanted to borrow more books.
He began to see himself in a new way.
He was proud of his bookmark.
qs.why: He had never thought of himself as brave before——他第一次觉得自己勇敢，对自己有了新的认识。

papers.label: 中考 · 说明文
papers.title: Why Do We Yawn?
paras: Everyone yawns. Babies yawn, and so do cats, dogs and even fish.
每个人都会打哈欠。婴儿会，猫、狗甚至鱼也会。
But why do we do it?
可我们为什么会打哈欠呢？
For a long time, people believed that we yawn because our bodies need more air.
很长时间里，人们认为打哈欠是因为身体需要更多空气。
However, many scientists now think this idea is not quite right.
不过，现在很多科学家认为这个说法不太对。
In some tests, people breathed air with extra oxygen, but they still yawned just as often.
在一些实验里，人们呼吸了含氧更多的空气，但打哈欠的次数一点没少。
Another idea is that yawning helps to cool the brain.
另一种说法是，打哈欠能帮助大脑降温。
When we open our mouths wide, cool air comes in, and more blood moves through the head.
我们把嘴张大时，凉空气进来，流过头部的血液也更多。
A cooler brain may help us stay awake and think clearly.
温度低一点的大脑也许能帮我们保持清醒、思路清楚。
This may explain why we often yawn when we are tired or bored.
这也许能解释，为什么我们累了或无聊时常常打哈欠。
Yawning is also catching.
打哈欠还会“传染”。
If you see a friend yawn, you will probably yawn too.
如果你看到朋友打哈欠，你很可能也会跟着打。
Some people even yawn when they read about yawning.
有些人甚至读到关于打哈欠的文字时也会打。
Did you yawn while reading this?
读这篇文章时，你打哈欠了吗？

qs.q: What did people believe about yawning for a long time?
qs.why: 第二段第一句：people believed that we yawn because our bodies need more air。

qs.q: What did the tests with extra oxygen show?
qs.why: they still yawned just as often——氧气多了，哈欠并没有少，所以“缺空气”的说法站不住。

qs.q: According to the passage, a cooler brain may help us ______.
qs.why: A cooler brain may help us stay awake and think clearly。

qs.q: What is the best title for the last paragraph?
qs.why: 最后一段讲 Yawning is also catching，看到、读到都会跟着打，即“会传染”。

papers.label: 高考 · 记叙文
papers.title: A Summer at the Bird Hospital
paras: When my mother suggested I volunteer at a wildlife rescue center last summer, I agreed mainly because it would look good on my college application.
去年夏天妈妈建议我去野生动物救助中心做志愿者，我答应了，主要是因为这会让我的大学申请好看一些。
I imagined holding baby animals and taking cute photos.
我想象着抱着小动物、拍些可爱的照片。
The reality was very different.
现实完全不是这样。
On my first morning, the manager handed me a bucket and a pair of gloves.
第一天早上，负责人递给我一只桶和一副手套。
My job was to clean the cages of injured seabirds, many of which had been caught in fishing lines.
我的工作是清理受伤海鸟的笼子，很多海鸟是被渔线缠住的。
The smell was terrible, and the birds were frightened of humans, so I was told never to touch them unless it was necessary.
气味很难闻，鸟又怕人，所以我被告知除非必要，绝不要碰它们。
By the end of the week, my arms ached and I had not taken a single photo.
到周末，我的胳膊酸痛，一张照片也没拍。
Things changed in my third week.
第三周，事情有了变化。
A young gull arrived with a damaged wing, and I was asked to record how much it ate each day.
一只翅膀受伤的小海鸥被送来，我负责记录它每天吃多少。
For days it refused food, and I began to fear the worst.
好几天它都不肯吃东西，我开始担心会有最坏的结果。
Then one morning the dish was empty.
后来有一天早上，食盘空了。
I was so excited that I ran to tell the vet, who simply smiled and said, "Now you understand why we do this."
我激动得跑去告诉兽医，她只是笑了笑说：“现在你明白我们为什么做这件事了。”
Six weeks later, we released the gull at the beach.
六周后，我们在海滩上放飞了那只海鸥。
It hesitated for a moment, then flew off without looking back.
它犹豫了一会儿，然后头也不回地飞走了。
I did mention the center in my application in the end, but not for the reason I had first planned.
最后我确实在申请里写了这个救助中心，但不是因为我最初打算的那个理由。
I wrote about patience, and about the joy of helping something that will never thank you.
我写的是耐心，以及帮助一个永远不会感谢你的生命时的那种快乐。

qs.q: Why did the author agree to volunteer at first?
o: To study to be a vet.
qs.why: 第一句：mainly because it would look good on my college application。

qs.q: What does the second paragraph mainly show?
o: The work was harder than expected.
qs.why: 又脏又累、鸟怕人、胳膊酸痛、一张照片没拍——和第一段的想象形成对比，说明工作比预想的辛苦。

qs.q: What does "I began to fear the worst" suggest?
o: The author was afraid of the gull.
The author thought the vet was wrong.
The author worried the gull might die.
qs.why: 海鸥连续几天不吃东西，fear the worst 指担心它会死。

qs.q: What did the author finally learn from the experience?
o: Helping others can be rewarding in itself.
Volunteering is a waste of time.
Photos are the best way to remember things.
qs.why: 最后一句：the joy of helping something that will never thank you——帮助本身就是回报。

papers.label: 高考 · 说明文
papers.title: Do Plants Talk to Each Other?
paras: Plants cannot walk, shout or run away from danger.
植物不会走，不会喊，也不能逃离危险。
Yet researchers are discovering that they are far from silent.
然而研究者发现，它们远不是沉默的。
Many plants seem to send warning signals to their neighbours.
很多植物似乎会向邻居发出警报信号。
When some plants are attacked by insects, they release special chemicals into the air.
有些植物被昆虫啃咬时，会向空气中释放特殊的化学物质。
Nearby plants that "smell" these chemicals often begin to produce substances that make their leaves taste bad, even before any insect arrives.
附近“闻到”这些物质的植物，往往在虫子还没来之前，就开始产生让叶子变难吃的物质。
In this way, one plant's bad luck becomes an early warning for others.
这样，一株植物的不幸就成了其他植物的预警。
Signals may also travel underground.
信号也可能在地下传递。
The roots of many trees are connected by fine threads of fungus that spread through the soil.
许多树的根被土壤里蔓延的细细的真菌菌丝连在一起。
Some scientists believe that water, food and even chemical messages can pass along this network, which has been nicknamed the "wood wide web".
一些科学家认为，水分、养料甚至化学信息都能沿着这个网络传递，它被戏称为“树联网”。
Not everyone agrees on how important these connections really are.
对于这些联系到底有多重要，并不是所有人都意见一致。
Critics point out that many experiments were done in laboratories or small areas, and results from real forests are harder to prove.
批评者指出，很多实验是在实验室或小范围内做的，真实森林里的结果更难证明。
Still, the research has changed the way many people see plants: not as lonely individuals, but as members of a busy community.
尽管如此，这些研究改变了很多人看待植物的方式：它们不是孤独的个体，而是一个忙碌群落中的成员。

qs.q: What happens when some plants are attacked by insects?
o: They release chemicals into the air.
qs.why: 第二段第一句：they release special chemicals into the air。

qs.q: The "wood wide web" refers to ______.
o: a network of fungus connecting roots
qs.why: 第三段：树根被真菌菌丝连起来，这个网络 has been nicknamed the "wood wide web"。

qs.q: What do critics think of the research?
o: Its results in real forests are hard to prove.
qs.why: Critics point out ... results from real forests are harder to prove——只是认为证据不足，并非全盘否定。

qs.q: What is the author's attitude toward the research?
qs.why: 作者介绍了发现，也写了批评意见，最后用 Still 肯定它改变了人们的看法——客观而有兴趣。

papers.label: 四级 · 仔细阅读
papers.title: Second-hand Is the New First Choice
paras: A few years ago, buying used goods was something many university students did quietly, almost with embarrassment.
几年前，买二手货是很多大学生悄悄做的事，甚至有点难为情。
Today, it has become a point of pride.
如今，这却成了一件值得骄傲的事。
On campuses across the country, second-hand markets, online exchange groups and "free shelves" in dormitories are more popular than ever.
在全国各地的校园里，二手市场、网上闲置交换群和宿舍里的“免费书架”比以往任何时候都受欢迎。
Money is the most obvious reason.
钱是最明显的原因。
A textbook that costs a hundred yuan new may sell for a third of that price after one semester.
一本新书要一百元的教材，用过一个学期后可能只卖三分之一的价钱。
For students living on a limited budget, the savings add up quickly.
对预算有限的学生来说，省下的钱很快就积少成多。
But price is not the whole story.
但价格并不是全部原因。
Many young people say they buy second-hand because they are worried about waste.
很多年轻人说，他们买二手货是因为担心浪费。
They have grown up hearing about climate change and plastic pollution, and they see reusing goods as a simple, practical way to act on their values.
他们从小就听说气候变化和塑料污染，把重复利用物品看作一种简单、实际的方式，来践行自己的价值观。
Selling an unwanted lamp or bicycle to a classmate feels better than throwing it away.
把不要的台灯或自行车卖给同学，总比扔掉感觉好。
The trend also reflects a change in how status is shown.
这种潮流也反映出人们展示身份的方式发生了变化。
For earlier generations, owning something brand-new was a sign of success.
对前几代人来说，拥有全新的东西是成功的标志。
For many students now, finding a rare jacket at a low price is a story worth sharing, and being a smart buyer matters more than being a big spender.
而对现在很多学生来说，低价淘到一件少见的夹克是值得分享的故事，会买比花得多更重要。
There are problems, of course.
当然，也存在问题。
Buyers sometimes find that goods are not as described, and online deals between strangers can lead to disputes.
买家有时发现东西和描述不符，陌生人之间的网上交易也可能引发纠纷。
Some universities have responded by setting up official exchange platforms with clear rules, hoping to keep the benefits while reducing the risks.
一些大学的做法是建立规则清楚的官方交换平台，希望在保留好处的同时降低风险。

qs.q: How did students feel about buying used goods a few years ago?
qs.why: 第一段：did quietly, almost with embarrassment。

qs.q: What does the example of the textbook show?
o: Second-hand books are of poor quality.
Textbooks are too expensive to buy.
Used goods can save students a lot of money.
qs.why: 新书一百元，用一学期后卖三分之一价，说明 the savings add up quickly。

qs.q: According to Paragraph 3, why do many young people choose second-hand goods?
o: They want to start a business.
qs.why: because they are worried about waste，把重复利用当作践行价值观的方式。

qs.q: What has changed about how status is shown?
o: Owning new things matters more than before.
Being a smart buyer is valued over spending a lot.
Students no longer care about status.
Rare jackets have become too expensive.
qs.why: 第四段末：being a smart buyer matters more than being a big spender。

qs.q: How have some universities responded to the problems?
o: By setting up official platforms with clear rules.
By warning students not to buy used goods.
qs.why: 最后一段：setting up official exchange platforms with clear rules。

papers.label: 四级 · 仔细阅读
papers.title: Sleep: The Study Tool Nobody Uses
paras: Ask students how they prepare for an important exam, and many will describe late nights, strong coffee and hours of reviewing notes.
问学生们怎样准备重要考试，很多人会说熬夜、浓咖啡和一连几个小时复习笔记。
Few will mention sleep.
很少有人会提到睡觉。
Yet a growing body of research suggests that sleep may be one of the most effective study tools available.
然而越来越多的研究表明，睡眠可能是现有最有效的学习工具之一。
While we sleep, the brain does not simply rest.
我们睡觉时，大脑并不只是在休息。
It replays and organizes information collected during the day, strengthening some memories and letting others fade.
它会重放、整理白天收集的信息，强化一部分记忆，让另一部分淡去。
In many experiments, people who learned a list of words and then slept remembered more of them the next day than people who stayed awake for the same length of time.
在许多实验中，背完一串单词后去睡觉的人，第二天记住的词比同样时长保持清醒的人更多。
Losing sleep has the opposite effect.
缺觉则会适得其反。
After a night without enough rest, it becomes harder to concentrate, and new information is less likely to be stored properly.
一夜没睡好之后，人更难集中注意力，新信息也更难被好好存进记忆里。
In other words, a student who stays up all night may have read more pages, but will probably remember less of what was on them.
换句话说，通宵的学生也许多读了几页书，但很可能记住的内容反而更少。
This does not mean that sleeping is a replacement for studying.
这并不意味着睡觉可以代替学习。
Memory needs something to work on.
记忆需要有材料可加工。
The most effective approach seems to combine the two: study in short sessions spread over several days, and protect regular sleep, especially on the night before the exam.
最有效的方法似乎是两者结合：把学习分成短时段，分散在几天里进行，同时保证规律的睡眠，尤其是考前那一晚。
Changing habits is not easy, particularly when friends are studying late and deadlines are close.
改变习惯并不容易，尤其是朋友们都在熬夜、截止日期又临近的时候。
But students who try going to bed on time often report that they feel calmer and think more clearly during exams, which may be the best reason of all to switch off the light.
但尝试按时睡觉的学生常说，考试时他们更平静、思路更清楚——这也许是关灯睡觉最好的理由。

qs.q: What does the author suggest about most students' exam preparation?
o: They pay too little attention to sleep.
qs.why: 第一段：Few will mention sleep，而研究表明睡眠是有效的学习工具。

qs.q: What happens in the brain during sleep?
o: It learns new words by itself.
It forgets everything learned that day.
qs.why: 第二段：replays and organizes information ... strengthening some memories。

qs.q: What does the experiment with word lists show?
o: Word lists are hard to learn.
qs.why: 学完后睡觉的人第二天记得更多。

qs.q: What is the author's main point in Paragraph 4?
o: Long study sessions are the most effective.
Spaced study and regular sleep work best together.
Students should study only on the night before an exam.
qs.why: combine the two：分散的短时段学习 + 规律睡眠。

qs.q: Why is it hard for students to change their habits?
o: Their friends study late and deadlines are close.
Teachers require them to stay up.
They do not believe the research.
qs.why: 最后一段第一句：particularly when friends are studying late and deadlines are close。

papers.label: 六级 · 仔细阅读
papers.title: The Hidden Price of Free Apps
paras: Most of the apps on our phones cost nothing to download.
我们手机上的大多数应用下载都不花钱。
We use them to chat, shop, navigate and pass the time, rarely stopping to ask how the companies behind them make money.
我们用它们聊天、购物、导航、打发时间，很少停下来想想背后的公司是怎么赚钱的。
The answer, in many cases, is that we are paying with something other than cash: our attention and our personal data.
在很多情况下，答案是我们在用现金以外的东西付费：我们的注意力和个人数据。
Every tap, search and pause on a screen can be recorded.
屏幕上的每一次点击、搜索和停留都可能被记录下来。
Combined, these details allow companies to build remarkably accurate profiles of their users, predicting what they are likely to buy, watch or believe.
这些细节汇总起来，能让公司为用户建立非常准确的画像，预测他们可能买什么、看什么、相信什么。
Such profiles are valuable to advertisers, who are willing to pay to reach exactly the right audience at exactly the right moment.
这种画像对广告商很有价值，他们愿意付钱，在恰当的时刻精准地触达恰当的人群。
Defenders of this model argue that it is a fair exchange.
这种模式的支持者认为，这是一种公平的交换。
Users receive useful services without opening their wallets, and the adverts they see are more relevant to their interests.
用户不用掏钱就能获得有用的服务，看到的广告也更符合自己的兴趣。
Without advertising, they point out, many services would have to charge fees that poorer users could not afford.
他们指出，没有广告的话，很多服务就得收费，而较穷的用户负担不起。
Critics are less convinced.
批评者则不那么信服。
They note that few people read the long privacy agreements they accept, so the "exchange" is hardly an informed one.
他们指出，很少有人会读自己同意的冗长隐私协议，因此这种“交换”很难说是知情的。
More worrying, apps designed to hold attention for as long as possible may encourage habits that users themselves would not choose, such as checking their phones late into the night.
更令人担忧的是，那些为尽可能长时间吸引注意力而设计的应用，可能会助长用户自己并不想要的习惯，比如深夜还在刷手机。
Some governments have begun to respond with rules requiring clearer consent and limits on how data can be shared.
一些政府已经开始出台规定，要求更明确的同意，并限制数据的共享方式。
Ultimately, however, the most effective protection may be awareness.
不过，归根结底，最有效的保护也许是意识。
An app may be free to install, but users who understand what they are giving up are in a far better position to decide whether the price is worth paying.
应用也许可以免费安装，但明白自己付出了什么的用户，才更有能力判断这个代价是否值得。

qs.q: According to the first paragraph, how do users pay for free apps?
o: With their attention and personal data.
qs.why: paying with something other than cash: our attention and our personal data。

qs.q: Why are user profiles valuable to advertisers?
o: They make users trust adverts more.
They reduce the cost of making apps.
They help advertisers reach the right audience.
qs.why: to reach exactly the right audience at exactly the right moment。

qs.q: What do defenders of the model argue?
o: Free services benefit users who cannot afford fees.
Privacy agreements are easy to understand.
Users should pay for every app.
qs.why: 没有广告，很多服务就要收费，poorer users could not afford——免费模式让穷用户也能用。

qs.q: Why do critics say the exchange is "hardly an informed one"?
o: Users rarely read the privacy agreements.
Apps do not have privacy agreements.
qs.why: few people read the long privacy agreements they accept。

qs.q: What does the author consider the most effective protection?
o: Users' awareness of what they give up.
qs.why: the most effective protection may be awareness。

papers.label: 六级 · 仔细阅读
papers.title: Why Cities Need More Shade
paras: On a hot summer afternoon, the temperature in a city centre can be several degrees higher than in the surrounding countryside.
炎热夏日的午后，市中心的气温可能比周边乡村高出好几度。
This effect, known as the urban heat island, is caused largely by the materials cities are built from.
这种现象被称为城市热岛效应，主要是由城市的建筑材料造成的。
Concrete, asphalt and brick absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly at night, so the city never fully cools down.
混凝土、沥青和砖白天吸收阳光，夜里慢慢释放热量，所以城市始终凉不下来。
The consequences go far beyond discomfort.
其后果远不止让人不舒服。
Extreme heat places a serious strain on the human body, especially for elderly people and those with heart conditions.
极端高温给人体带来很大负担，对老年人和心脏病患者尤其如此。
It also drives up demand for air conditioning, which consumes large amounts of electricity and, ironically, pumps even more heat into the streets.
它还推高了空调需求，而空调耗电量很大，具有讽刺意味的是，还会把更多热量排到街上。
Trees offer one of the simplest remedies.
树木是最简单的解决办法之一。
Their leaves block sunlight before it reaches the ground, and the water they release through their leaves cools the surrounding air, much as sweat cools our skin.
树叶在阳光到达地面之前就把它挡住，树通过叶片释放的水分又能给周围空气降温，就像汗水给皮肤降温一样。
A street lined with mature trees can feel dramatically cooler than a bare one only a few blocks away.
一条种满大树的街道，会比几个街区外光秃秃的街道凉快得多。
Planting trees, however, is not as straightforward as it sounds.
然而种树并不像听起来那么简单。
Young trees need years to grow large enough to provide real shade, and many die early because of poor soil, limited space for roots or a lack of watering.
小树要长很多年才能大到真正遮阴，很多树还会因为土壤差、根系空间有限或缺少浇水而早早死去。
There is also a question of fairness: wealthier neighbourhoods tend to have far more green cover than poorer ones, where residents may need shade the most.
还有公平问题：富裕社区的绿化往往远多于贫困社区，而后者的居民可能最需要树荫。
For these reasons, experts argue that cities should treat trees not as decoration but as essential infrastructure, like roads or water pipes, with long-term budgets for care.
因此，专家认为城市应该把树木当作必要的基础设施，而不是装饰，就像道路或水管一样，为养护安排长期预算。
As summers grow hotter, shade may turn out to be one of the most valuable public resources a city can offer.
随着夏天越来越热，树荫也许会成为一座城市能提供的最宝贵的公共资源之一。

qs.q: What mainly causes the urban heat island effect?
o: The materials used to build cities.
A lack of rain in summer.
qs.why: caused largely by the materials cities are built from。

qs.q: Why does the author call the use of air conditioning "ironic"?
o: It is rarely used in cities.
It is too expensive for most people.
It is bad for elderly people.
It adds more heat to the streets it is meant to escape.
qs.why: 为了躲热而开空调，空调却把更多热量排到街上，所以说 ironically。

qs.q: How do trees cool the air, according to Paragraph 3?
o: By blocking sunlight and releasing water.
qs.why: leaves block sunlight，以及 the water they release ... cools the surrounding air。

qs.q: What fairness problem does the author mention?
o: Trees are more expensive in poor areas.
Rich people plant too many trees.
Poorer areas often have fewer trees.
Only rich areas suffer from heat.
qs.why: wealthier neighbourhoods tend to have far more green cover than poorer ones。

qs.q: What do experts suggest cities should do?
qs.why: treat trees not as decoration but as essential infrastructure。

papers.label: 考研英语 · 阅读 Part A
papers.title: The Productivity Puzzle of Working from Home
paras: When offices emptied almost overnight a few years ago, many managers predicted a collapse in productivity.
几年前办公室几乎在一夜之间人去楼空时，很多管理者预言生产率会大幅下滑。
Without supervisors nearby, they assumed, employees would drift into distraction.
他们以为，没有上司在旁边，员工就会三心二意。
The collapse never came.
然而下滑从未出现。
Many firms reported that output held steady or even rose, and a large share of workers said they never wanted to return to a daily commute.
很多公司报告产出保持稳定甚至上升，相当一部分员工表示再也不想回到每天通勤的日子。
Yet the debate has proved far from settled.
可这场争论远未尘埃落定。
Part of the difficulty lies in what is being measured.
部分困难在于衡量的是什么。
Tasks that can be counted, such as calls answered or reports completed, often look healthy at home.
那些能计数的任务，比如接了多少电话、完成了多少报告，在家办公时往往数据不错。

What is harder to count is the informal exchange of ideas: the overheard conversation, the quick question at a colleague's desk, the advice a junior employee picks up simply by watching how experienced staff handle a difficult client.
更难统计的是非正式的想法交流：无意间听到的谈话、到同事桌前问的一个小问题，以及年轻员工仅仅通过观察有经验的同事如何应对难缠客户而学到的东西。
These gains are slow to appear and easy to overlook, which is precisely why they matter.
这些收获出现得慢，又容易被忽视，而这正是它们重要的原因。
A company may enjoy higher output this year while quietly weakening the training of the people who will run it in ten years.
一家公司今年也许产出更高，却在不知不觉中削弱了对十年后掌管公司的那批人的培养。
Some evidence suggests that younger workers, who have the most to learn, are also the ones who lose most when teams rarely meet in person.
有证据表明，最需要学习的年轻员工，恰恰也是团队很少当面见面时损失最大的人。
None of this amounts to a case for forcing everyone back to their desks five days a week.
这一切并不构成强迫所有人每周五天回到工位的理由。
Commuting costs time and money, and flexibility allows companies to recruit people who could never live near an expensive city centre.
通勤耗费时间和金钱，而灵活办公让公司能招到那些永远住不起昂贵市中心附近的人。
The more sensible conclusion is that the question "Is remote work productive?" is too crude to be useful.
更合理的结论是，“远程办公有没有效率？”这个问题太粗糙，没有什么用处。
The better question is which kinds of work, and which stages of a career, benefit from being together, and how organizations can design their weeks around the answer.
更好的问题是：哪些类型的工作、职业生涯的哪些阶段，能从在一起办公中受益，以及组织如何围绕这个答案来安排每周的工作。

qs.q: What did many managers expect when offices first emptied?
qs.why: 第一段：predicted a collapse in productivity，以为没人监督员工会分心。

qs.q: According to Paragraph 2, the debate remains unsettled partly because ______.
o: workers refuse to report their output
some valuable activities are hard to measure
qs.why: Part of the difficulty lies in what is being measured——非正式交流 is harder to count。

qs.q: The author mentions younger workers in Paragraph 3 to show that ______.
o: they are less productive than older staff
the costs of remote work may fall unevenly
they should be trained by computers
qs.why: 最需要学习的年轻人 lose most——远程办公的代价并非平均分摊。

qs.q: Which of the following best describes the author's view?
o: Productivity cannot be measured at all.
The question needs to be asked in a more precise way.
qs.why: 第四段：原问题 too crude to be useful，应该问哪些工作、哪些职业阶段适合在一起。

qs.q: The best title for the text could be ______.
qs.why: 全文核心：只看可计数的产出不够，还要看难以衡量的学习与交流——超越“数产出”。

papers.label: 考研英语 · 阅读 Part A
papers.title: Whose Treasures Are They?
paras: Walk through the great museums of Europe and North America and you will find objects gathered from every corner of the world: statues, manuscripts, ceremonial masks, entire sections of ancient buildings.
走进欧洲和北美的大博物馆，你会看到来自世界各个角落的物品：雕像、手稿、祭祀面具，甚至古建筑的整段构件。
For generations these collections were presented as evidence of a shared human heritage.
几代人以来，这些藏品一直被当作全人类共同遗产的证据来展示。
Increasingly, they are also seen as evidence of something less comfortable.
而越来越多的人也把它们看作另一种不那么光彩的证据。
Many such objects left their places of origin during periods of conquest or colonial rule, when the people who made them had little power to refuse.
许多这类物品是在征服或殖民统治时期离开原产地的，那时制造它们的人几乎无力拒绝。
Governments and communities in those regions have long asked for their return, and in recent years a number of museums have agreed.
这些地区的政府和社群长期要求归还，近年来已有一些博物馆同意了。

Supporters of return argue that a sculpture removed from a temple loses much of its meaning when displayed behind glass thousands of miles away, and that ownership acquired through force carries no moral weight.
支持归还的人认为，从神庙里搬走的雕塑，摆在千里之外的玻璃柜里就失去了大部分意义；而且通过武力获得的所有权没有道德分量。
Museums that resist often make two arguments.
持反对态度的博物馆通常有两个论点。
The first is practical: they claim to possess the expertise and facilities to preserve fragile objects, and that more visitors can see them in a major city.
第一个是现实层面的：它们声称自己具备保护脆弱文物的专业能力和设施，而且在大城市能有更多人看到。
The second is philosophical: a "universal museum", they say, allows visitors to compare cultures side by side, an experience no single national collection can offer.
第二个是理念层面的：它们说，“普世博物馆”让参观者能把不同文化放在一起比较，这是任何单一国家的收藏都无法提供的体验。
Neither argument is as strong as it once seemed.
这两个论点都不像过去看起来那么有力了。

Many countries of origin now run well-equipped museums of their own, and the claim that great art is best appreciated in a handful of wealthy capitals sounds uncomfortably like the attitudes that justified taking it in the first place.
许多原产国如今都有设施完善的博物馆；而“伟大的艺术最适合在少数几个富裕首都欣赏”的说法，听起来令人不安地像当初为拿走它们辩护的那种态度。
A more promising path may lie between the extremes: long-term loans, shared research, and exhibitions that travel in both directions.
更有希望的出路也许在两个极端之间：长期出借、共同研究，以及双向巡展。
Such arrangements treat the question not as a contest over possession but as an opportunity to rebuild trust.
这样的安排不把问题看作一场争夺所有权的较量，而是看作重建信任的机会。

qs.q: The phrase "something less comfortable" (Para. 1) most probably refers to ______.
o: a history of unequal power and taking
the high cost of maintaining museums
qs.why: 第二段解释：很多文物是在征服或殖民时期、原主无力拒绝时离开的——即不平等的掠取史。

qs.q: Supporters of return believe that ______.
o: museums should charge higher entrance fees
an object may lose meaning outside its original setting
ownership is decided by who preserves an object best
objects should be shown in as many cities as possible
qs.why: a sculpture removed from a temple loses much of its meaning when displayed behind glass。

qs.q: The "universal museum" argument stresses the value of ______.
qs.why: allows visitors to compare cultures side by side。

qs.q: What does the author imply about the claim that great art is best seen in wealthy capitals?
o: It explains why museums are popular.
It echoes attitudes that once justified taking the objects.
It is accepted by most countries of origin.
It is supported by recent research.
qs.why: sounds uncomfortably like the attitudes that justified taking it in the first place。

qs.q: The author's attitude toward long-term loans and shared exhibitions is ______.
qs.why: A more promising path ... an opportunity to rebuild trust——态度积极、有希望。

papers.label: 雅思 · 学术类阅读
papers.title: A Short History of the Umbrella
paras: The umbrella is so ordinary that we rarely give it a second thought, yet its history stretches back thousands of years.
雨伞平常得让我们很少多想它一眼，但它的历史可以追溯到几千年前。
The earliest versions were not designed for rain at all.
最早的伞根本不是为挡雨设计的。
Carvings and paintings from ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia and China show servants holding shades over the heads of kings and nobles to protect them from the sun.
古埃及、美索不达米亚和中国的雕刻与绘画中，都有仆人为国王和贵族撑伞遮阳的画面。
In these societies the shade was a mark of rank: the more important the person, the larger and more richly decorated it tended to be.
在这些社会里，伞是身份的标志：人物越重要，伞往往越大、装饰越华丽。
It was in China that waterproof umbrellas are believed to have first become common.
人们认为防水的伞最早是在中国普及的。
By coating paper or silk with oil or wax, craftsmen produced canopies that could shed water, and the folding frame made of bamboo allowed the device to be carried easily.
工匠在纸或丝绸上涂油或蜡，做出能防水的伞面，竹制的折叠伞骨又让伞便于携带。
Oiled-paper umbrellas remain a traditional craft in parts of East Asia today.
如今在东亚一些地方，油纸伞仍是一门传统手艺。
In Europe, by contrast, the umbrella was slow to win acceptance.
相比之下，伞在欧洲很久才被接受。
For much of the eighteenth century it was regarded in Britain as a feminine accessory, and a man carrying one in the rain risked being laughed at in the street.
在十八世纪的大部分时间里，英国人把伞看作女性的配饰，男人下雨天打伞可能会在街上被人嘲笑。
Drivers of horse-drawn cabs were particularly hostile, since every umbrella represented a passenger who might otherwise have paid for a ride.
马车车夫尤其反感，因为每多一把伞，就可能少一位本来会付钱坐车的乘客。
Attitudes changed only gradually, as more people, men included, decided that staying dry mattered more than public opinion.
态度只是慢慢改变，越来越多的人——包括男人——认为保持干爽比别人的看法更重要。
The modern umbrella owes much to the industrial age.
现代雨伞在很大程度上要归功于工业时代。
In the nineteenth century, heavy frames of wood and whalebone were replaced by lighter steel ribs, making umbrellas cheaper, stronger and available to almost everyone.
十九世纪，木头和鲸须做的沉重伞骨被更轻的钢制伞骨取代，伞变得更便宜、更结实，几乎人人都买得起。
Later developments, such as compact folding designs and automatic opening, were refinements rather than revolutions.
后来的发展，比如可折叠的小型设计和自动开伞，只是改良，而不是革命。
Remarkably, the basic shape, a fabric canopy stretched over a central shaft, has hardly changed in three thousand years.
值得一提的是，伞的基本形态——一根中轴上撑开一块布面——三千年来几乎没变。

qs.q: What was the main purpose of the earliest umbrellas?
o: To shade important people from the sun.
qs.why: 第一段：最早的伞 not designed for rain，是为国王贵族遮阳的。

qs.q: What made Chinese umbrellas waterproof?
o: A coating of oil or wax.
qs.why: 第二段：coating paper or silk with oil or wax。

qs.q: Why did cab drivers dislike umbrellas?
qs.why: every umbrella represented a passenger who might otherwise have paid for a ride。

qs.q: What did the nineteenth century contribute to the umbrella?
o: Lighter steel frames that lowered the price.
qs.why: lighter steel ribs, making umbrellas cheaper, stronger。自动开伞是后来的改良。

qs.q: What point does the writer make in the final sentence?
o: Umbrellas were invented three thousand years ago in Europe.
Modern umbrellas are of poor quality.
The umbrella's basic design has stayed almost the same.
qs.why: the basic shape ... has hardly changed in three thousand years。

papers.label: 雅思 · 学术类阅读
papers.title: Too Many Bees on the Roof?
paras: Over the past two decades, beekeeping has become fashionable in many large cities.
过去二十年，养蜂在很多大城市成了一种时尚。
Hives have appeared on the roofs of hotels, offices and museums, and companies advertise their own honey as proof of their environmental credentials.
酒店、写字楼和博物馆的屋顶上出现了蜂箱，企业还把自家产的蜂蜜当作环保形象的证明来宣传。
The motivation is usually admirable: news of declining bee populations has persuaded many people that keeping bees is a direct way to help.
动机通常是好的：蜜蜂数量减少的新闻让很多人相信，养蜂是直接帮忙的办法。
Ecologists, however, have begun to point out a misunderstanding.
然而生态学家开始指出其中的误解。
The honeybee is only one of thousands of bee species, and it is not the one most at risk.
蜜蜂只是几千种蜂中的一种，而且不是最濒危的那种。
Managed by beekeepers and bred in large numbers, honeybees are in effect farm animals.
蜜蜂由养蜂人管理、大量繁育，实际上相当于家畜。
Many wild bees, by contrast, live alone or in small colonies, nest in the ground or in hollow stems, and depend on particular kinds of flowers.
相比之下，许多野生蜂独居或组成小群落，在地里或空心的茎秆里筑巢，依赖特定种类的花。
It is these species whose numbers have fallen most sharply.
数量下降最厉害的正是这些物种。
When hives become too dense, the two groups may come into conflict.
蜂箱太密集时，两类蜂之间可能产生冲突。
A single colony can contain tens of thousands of workers, all searching for nectar and pollen.
一个蜂群可能有几万只工蜂，全都在寻找花蜜和花粉。
In areas where flowers are limited, such as dense city centres, honeybees may take resources that wild bees need.
在花朵有限的地方，比如密集的市中心，蜜蜂可能会抢走野生蜂需要的资源。
Some studies have also raised concerns that diseases carried by managed bees can spread to wild populations.
一些研究还担心，人工饲养的蜜蜂携带的疾病可能传给野生种群。
None of this means that urban beekeeping should be banned.
这并不意味着应该禁止城市养蜂。

Instead, researchers suggest that the most useful thing city dwellers can do is plant a wide variety of flowering plants, leave some areas of bare soil and dead wood, and reduce the use of pesticides.
研究者反而建议，城市居民能做的最有用的事是种植多样的开花植物，留出一些裸露的土地和枯木，并减少农药的使用。
These measures benefit honeybees and wild bees alike, and unlike a rooftop hive, they do not add to the competition for food.
这些措施对蜜蜂和野生蜂都有好处，而且不像屋顶蜂箱那样，会加剧对食物的争夺。

qs.q: Why have many people in cities started keeping bees?
o: To reduce the number of wild bees.
They believe it helps declining bee populations.
qs.why: 第一段：news of declining bee populations has persuaded many people that keeping bees is a direct way to help。

qs.q: According to the writer, which bees are most at risk?
qs.why: 蜜蜂 not the one most at risk；It is these species（野生蜂）whose numbers have fallen most sharply。

qs.q: Why does the writer describe honeybees as "farm animals"?
o: They eat the same food as cows.
They are managed and bred in large numbers by people.
qs.why: Managed by beekeepers and bred in large numbers。

qs.q: What problem can occur when there are too many hives?
o: Honeybees may take food that wild bees need.
qs.why: honeybees may take resources that wild bees need。

qs.q: What do researchers recommend?
o: Planting diverse flowers and reducing pesticides.
Moving wild bees to the countryside.
qs.why: 最后一段：plant a wide variety of flowering plants ... reduce the use of pesticides。

papers.label: 托福 · 学术阅读
papers.title: Desert Varnish
paras: In many of the world's dry regions, cliffs and boulders are covered with a thin, dark coating that gives them a shiny brown or black appearance.
在世界上许多干旱地区，悬崖和巨石上覆盖着一层薄薄的深色涂层，使它们呈现出有光泽的棕色或黑色。
Geologists call this coating desert varnish.
地质学家称这层涂层为“荒漠漆”。
Although it is usually less than a fraction of a millimeter thick, it can dramatically change the color of an entire landscape.
虽然它通常只有零点几毫米厚，却能大大改变整片地貌的颜色。
Chemical analysis shows that desert varnish consists largely of clay minerals together with oxides of manganese and iron.
化学分析表明，荒漠漆主要由黏土矿物以及锰和铁的氧化物组成。
The manganese is especially puzzling.
锰尤其令人费解。
It is often present in the varnish at concentrations many times higher than in the rock underneath or in the surrounding dust, which means it cannot simply have leaked out of the stone.
它在荒漠漆中的浓度往往比下面的岩石或周围的尘土高出许多倍，这说明它不可能只是从石头里渗出来的。
Some process must be concentrating it at the surface.
一定有某种过程把它富集到了表面。
Scientists have proposed two main explanations.
科学家提出了两种主要解释。
According to the biological hypothesis, microorganisms living on rock surfaces absorb manganese from dust and moisture and deposit it as they grow.
按照生物假说，生活在岩石表面的微生物从尘土和水汽中吸收锰，并在生长过程中把它沉积下来。
Supporters point out that bacteria capable of this have been found in varnish samples.
支持者指出，在荒漠漆样本中已经发现了有这种能力的细菌。
The chemical hypothesis, in contrast, holds that manganese becomes concentrated through repeated cycles of wetting and drying, without any help from living things.
相反，化学假说认为，锰是在反复的湿润和干燥循环中富集起来的，并不需要生物的帮助。
Critics of the biological view note that the microorganisms are relatively rare, while critics of the chemical view argue that it fails to explain why varnish forms so unevenly.
生物假说的批评者指出这些微生物比较少见，而化学假说的批评者则认为它解释不了荒漠漆为什么形成得如此不均匀。
Whatever its origin, desert varnish forms extremely slowly, perhaps taking thousands of years to become fully dark.
无论成因如何，荒漠漆的形成极其缓慢，可能要几千年才能完全变暗。
This slowness has made it useful to archaeologists.
这种缓慢使它对考古学家很有用。
Ancient peoples in many deserts created images by scratching through the varnish to expose the lighter rock beneath.
许多沙漠中的古代人通过刮开荒漠漆、露出下面颜色较浅的岩石来作画。
Over time, new varnish gradually darkens these images, and the degree of darkening offers a rough indication of their age, although researchers continue to debate how reliable such estimates are.
随着时间推移，新的荒漠漆会使这些图像慢慢变暗，变暗的程度可以粗略地表明它们的年代，不过研究者对这类估算有多可靠仍有争议。

qs.q: According to paragraph 1, which of the following is true of desert varnish?
o: It is found only on cliffs.
It can change the appearance of a whole landscape.
It is lighter than the rock beneath it.
qs.why: it can dramatically change the color of an entire landscape。

qs.q: Why does the author consider the manganese in desert varnish "puzzling"?
o: It is absent from most samples.
It is much more concentrated than in the rock or dust.
qs.why: concentrations many times higher than in the rock underneath or in the surrounding dust。

qs.q: The word "deposit" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
qs.why: deposit 在这里是“沉积、放下”，即 lay down。

qs.q: What criticism is made of the chemical hypothesis?
o: It cannot explain the uneven formation of varnish.
It ignores the role of dust.
qs.why: it fails to explain why varnish forms so unevenly。“微生物稀少”是对生物假说的批评。

qs.q: Why is desert varnish useful to archaeologists?
o: Its slow darkening helps estimate the age of rock images.
It shows where ancient peoples found water.
qs.why: the degree of darkening offers a rough indication of their age。

papers.label: 托福 · 学术阅读
papers.title: How Coral Atolls Form
paras: Coral reefs are built by tiny animals called coral polyps, which take calcium from seawater to construct hard skeletons.
珊瑚礁是由叫作珊瑚虫的微小动物建造的，它们从海水中吸取钙来构建坚硬的骨骼。
Over many generations, these skeletons accumulate into massive structures.
经过许多代，这些骨骼堆积成巨大的结构。
Because reef-building corals depend on algae that need sunlight, they can grow only in warm, shallow, clear water.
由于造礁珊瑚依赖需要阳光的藻类，它们只能生长在温暖、清澈的浅水中。
Reefs take several forms.
珊瑚礁有几种形态。
Fringing reefs grow directly along a coastline.
岸礁紧贴着海岸线生长。
Barrier reefs also follow a coast but are separated from it by a wide lagoon.
堡礁也沿着海岸分布，但与海岸之间隔着宽阔的潟湖。
Atolls are the most striking of all: rings of coral, often broken into small islands, enclosing a lagoon in the open ocean with no land in the middle at all.
环礁是其中最引人注目的：一圈珊瑚，常常断开成一个个小岛，在开阔的大洋中围出一片潟湖，而中间根本没有陆地。
Since corals cannot grow in deep water, the existence of atolls rising from the deep sea floor presented early naturalists with a genuine mystery.
既然珊瑚不能在深水里生长，那些从深海海底升起的环礁的存在，就成了早期博物学家面前一个真正的谜。
In the nineteenth century, Charles Darwin proposed an elegant solution.
十九世纪，查尔斯·达尔文提出了一个巧妙的解释。
He suggested that each atoll began as a fringing reef around a volcanic island.
他认为，每个环礁最初都是火山岛周围的一圈岸礁。
As the volcano became inactive, the island slowly sank, but the corals kept growing upward toward the light, so that the reef stayed near the surface.
火山停止活动后，岛屿慢慢下沉，但珊瑚不断向上朝着光生长，因此礁石一直保持在海面附近。
With time, the fringing reef became a barrier reef separated from the shrinking island, and eventually, when the island disappeared beneath the waves entirely, only a ring of coral remained.
随着时间推移，岸礁变成了与日渐缩小的岛屿相隔的堡礁；最后，当岛屿完全沉入海面以下，只剩下一圈珊瑚。
Darwin had no way to test his idea directly, and for decades it remained controversial.
达尔文没有办法直接验证他的想法，几十年里它一直有争议。
Confirmation came in the twentieth century, when deep drilling on a Pacific atoll passed through more than a kilometer of coral limestone before striking volcanic rock.
直到二十世纪，在太平洋一个环礁上的深钻穿过了一千多米的珊瑚石灰岩，才打到火山岩，这一理论得到了证实。
Because corals grow only in shallow water, such a thick layer could have formed only if the base had been sinking steadily for millions of years, exactly as Darwin had predicted.
由于珊瑚只在浅水中生长，这么厚的一层只有在基底持续下沉数百万年的情况下才可能形成，这正如达尔文所预言的那样。

qs.q: Why can reef-building corals grow only in shallow water?
o: They depend on algae that need sunlight.
qs.why: depend on algae that need sunlight，所以只能在温暖、清澈的浅水中生长。

qs.q: What distinguishes an atoll from a barrier reef?
o: An atoll is found only in cold water.
An atoll grows directly along a coast.
An atoll has no land in its center.
An atoll is made of volcanic rock.
qs.why: 环礁 enclosing a lagoon ... with no land in the middle at all。

qs.q: Why did atolls present early naturalists with a mystery?
o: They are found far from volcanoes.
They appear to rise from water too deep for corals to grow.
qs.why: corals cannot grow in deep water，环礁却从深海海底升起。

qs.q: According to Darwin, what happened as the volcanic island sank?
o: The corals kept growing upward and stayed near the surface.
qs.why: the corals kept growing upward toward the light, so that the reef stayed near the surface。

qs.q: Why does the author mention the deep drilling in paragraph 4?
o: To describe how coral is mined.
To show that Darwin's theory was wrong.
To give evidence that supported Darwin's explanation.
qs.why: 钻穿一千多米珊瑚石灰岩才见火山岩，证明基底长期下沉——exactly as Darwin had predicted。

papers.label: GRE · Reading Comprehension
papers.title: The Stretching of a Concept
paras: The term "keystone species" entered ecology through a series of experiments in which researchers removed a single predatory sea star from rocky tide pools.
“关键种”这个术语是通过一系列实验进入生态学的：研究者从岩石潮池中移除了一种捕食性海星。
Freed from predation, mussels spread rapidly and crowded out many other organisms, so that the diversity of the community collapsed.
没有了捕食，贻贝迅速扩散，排挤掉了许多其他生物，群落的多样性随之崩溃。
The sea star, though not especially abundant, was thus holding the entire structure in place, much as a keystone holds an arch.
这种海星虽然数量并不特别多，却撑住了整个结构，就像拱顶石撑住拱门一样。
The metaphor proved enormously popular, and its success has come at a cost.
这个比喻大受欢迎，而它的成功也付出了代价。

Over the following decades, the label was applied to an ever-widening range of organisms, from large herbivores to plants to soil microbes, often on the strength of little more than the observation that they seemed important.
此后几十年里，这个标签被用到越来越多的生物上，从大型食草动物到植物再到土壤微生物，依据往往不过是它们“看起来很重要”。
Since nearly every species affects its community to some degree, a concept that can include almost anything risks explaining almost nothing.
既然几乎每个物种都会在某种程度上影响其群落，一个几乎什么都能装进去的概念，就有几乎什么都解释不了的风险。
Defenders of the broader usage reply that its vagueness is a practical virtue: a memorable label can mobilize public support for conservation in a way that technical language cannot.
支持宽泛用法的人回应说，它的模糊恰恰是一种实际优点：一个好记的标签能动员公众支持保护工作，这是专业术语做不到的。

The objection, however, is not that the term is used in public debate but that its looseness can mislead scientists themselves, encouraging the assumption that protecting one celebrated species will safeguard an ecosystem whose workings remain poorly understood.
然而，反对意见并不是说这个词被用于公共讨论，而是说它的松散会误导科学家本身，助长一种假设：只要保护一个出名的物种，就能保住一个运作机制仍然知之甚少的生态系统。

qs.q: The author mentions the sea star experiments primarily in order to ______.
o: show that mussels are harmful to tide pools
criticize the methods of early ecologists
argue that sea stars are the most important predators
describe the original, specific sense of a term
qs.why: 第一段交代“关键种”最初的具体含义：数量不多却维系整个群落结构。

qs.q: The author's main concern about the broader use of "keystone species" is that it ______.
o: is too technical for the public
qs.why: a concept that can include almost anything risks explaining almost nothing——失去了解释力。

qs.q: In the last paragraph, the author responds to the defenders' argument by ______.
o: conceding that the term should be abandoned
shifting the focus to the term's effect on scientific thinking
denying that the term helps conservation
qs.why: The objection ... is not that the term is used in public debate but that its looseness can mislead scientists themselves。

qs.q: Which of the following, if true, would most strengthen the author's position?
o: Technical terms are rarely used in news reports.
Public donations increased after the term became popular.
Sea stars remain common in many tide pools.
Several ecosystems declined even though the species labeled "keystone" in them were protected.
qs.why: 作者担心“保护一个明星物种就能保住生态系统”的假设会误导人；这个事实正说明了该假设不可靠。

papers.label: GRE · Reading Comprehension
papers.title: Diaries as Historical Evidence
paras: Historians have long prized private diaries as windows onto the past that are free from the distortions of official records.
历史学家一向珍视私人日记，把它看作通向过去的窗口，不受官方记录的扭曲。
A government report may be written to impress superiors, the reasoning goes, but a diary is written for no one but its author and is therefore more likely to be candid.
其逻辑是：政府报告可能是为了给上级留下好印象而写的，日记却只写给作者自己，因此更可能坦率。
This assumption deserves more scrutiny than it usually receives.
这个假设应当受到比通常更多的审视。

Many diarists in earlier centuries expected their journals to be read, by family members, by later generations, or even by the public after their death, and some revised their entries years afterward with that audience in mind.
早年许多写日记的人预料到日记会被人读到——被家人、被后代，甚至在他们死后被公众读到——有些人还在多年后带着这种读者意识修改过日记。
Even a diary never intended for other eyes is shaped by its writer's desire to make sense of events, to justify choices, or simply to present a more coherent self than daily life provides.
即使一本从未打算给别人看的日记，也受到作者种种愿望的塑造：想理解发生的事，想为自己的选择辩护，或者只是想呈现一个比日常生活更连贯的自我。
None of this makes diaries worthless; it makes them evidence of a particular kind.
这一切并不让日记变得毫无价值；只是让它成为一种特定类型的证据。
A diary may be unreliable as a record of what happened and yet highly revealing about how its author wished to understand what happened.
日记作为“发生了什么”的记录可能不可靠，却能深刻揭示作者希望如何理解所发生的事。
The historian's task is not to trust or distrust such sources wholesale but to ask, in each case, what question the document is actually able to answer.
历史学家的任务不是对这类资料全盘相信或全盘怀疑，而是在每个具体情况中追问：这份文献究竟能回答什么问题。

qs.q: The "assumption" referred to at the beginning of the second paragraph is that diaries ______.
o: are more candid than official records
are less interesting than government reports
qs.why: 指第一段的观点：日记只写给自己，所以 more likely to be candid。

qs.q: The author suggests that diarists sometimes revised their entries because they ______.
qs.why: some revised their entries years afterward with that audience in mind。

qs.q: According to the passage, a diary that is inaccurate about events may still be valuable as evidence of ______.
o: the opinions of the author's family
how its author wished to interpret events
qs.why: highly revealing about how its author wished to understand what happened。

qs.q: Which best describes the author's overall position?
o: Diaries should be rejected as historical sources.
Diaries are more reliable than any other source.
The value of a diary depends on the question the historian asks of it.
qs.why: 最后一句：ask, in each case, what question the document is actually able to answer。
